title: Brand brain
hired_for: To keep one true, signed record of the brand that every agent and person works from, so nothing is said or built that is false, off-brand or already decided.

jobs.job: Give every agent and freelancer the same true facts before they write or build anything
jobs.why: When each writer, designer or agent works from their own notes, drafts come back with the wrong price, the wrong tone or a product we stopped selling. The founder then spends hours fixing work that should have been right the first time.

watch.metric: agent and team outputs rejected for a brand reason (wrong fact, off-voice, already decided), share of all reviewed outputs, 30 days

drives.metric: outputs approved on the first pass

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 31% of drafts are sent back for a brand reason. After: under 10% within 60 days, once every agent loads the brain first.
jobs.who_today: founder, by memory and by rewriting drafts

jobs.job: Catch it when the site changes a price, offer or policy and the rest of the team does not know
jobs.why: A price or returns policy that changed on the site but not in the brain ends up in ads and emails as a promise we no longer keep. Shoppers see one number in the ad and another at checkout, and some ask for refunds or never buy.

watch.metric: facts that differ between the brain and the live site (price, offer, guarantee, shipping, returns), count, weekly site check
watch.source: brand brain site check against Shopify

drives.metric: support tickets about a price or policy that did not match, per 100 orders

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 7 facts differ, including a free shipping line the site dropped 3 weeks ago. After: 0 open differences, each one fixed or confirmed within 2 days.
jobs.who_today: nobody; found when a customer complains

jobs.job: Stop any claim we cannot prove from reaching an ad, email or page
jobs.why: An unproven claim like 'lasts 5 years' or 'best in the US' can get ads rejected, trigger refunds and draw legal letters. The brain keeps each claim with its proof, or marks it off limits.

watch.metric: share of claims in live ads and pages that have proof on file
watch.source: brand brain claims list matched to Meta ads and site pages

drives.metric: ads rejected or limited by Meta for a claim, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 58 of 90 live claims have proof on file (64%). After: 84 of 90 (93%) within 30 days; the other 6 are reworded or removed.
jobs.who_today: founder or agency, case by case

jobs.job: Stop agents and the team from reopening decisions I already made
jobs.why: Without a dated record of what was decided and why, the same rejected idea comes back every few weeks. Each time it costs a meeting and the founder's patience.

watch.metric: proposals that repeat an idea already rejected, count, 30 days

drives.metric: founder hours spent reviewing proposals per week (proxy: proposals reviewed per week)

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 6 repeat proposals a month, including free gifts over $50 twice. After: 0 or 1 a month, each one flagged with the old decision and its reason.
jobs.who_today: founder, by memory

jobs.job: Keep the margin floor and cost facts in one place so no offer loses money
jobs.why: Agents and agencies who do not know product cost, shipping cost and the lowest price we accept will suggest discounts that sell well and lose money on every order.

watch.metric: offers proposed below the margin floor, count, 30 days
watch.source: brand brain offer rules checked against Shopify product cost

drives.metric: gross margin after discounts

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 4 of 12 proposed offers in a month break the floor before anyone checks. After: 0 reach the founder; each is flagged with the margin it would leave.
jobs.who_today: founder or finance lead, in a spreadsheet

jobs.job: Hold the lines we never cross, and block any work that crosses them
jobs.why: Every brand has rules like never naming a rival, never going below 20% off or never using a model's face without consent. If they live only in the founder's head, someone breaks them.

watch.metric: outputs blocked because they broke a written red line, count, 30 days

drives.metric: ads and pages pulled after going live for a rule break

jobs.now_after: Example: Now red lines are unwritten and 2 ads went live last quarter naming a competitor. After: 12 red lines written and signed; breaks are caught before launch.
jobs.who_today: founder, by memory

jobs.job: Show me in one short list the questions only I can answer
jobs.why: The site, the ads and the data cannot tell the system who the brand is for, what it will never do or which product it is betting on. Until those answers exist, agents guess.

watch.metric: open questions waiting on the founder, count and age of the oldest in days

drives.metric: share of brain sections complete

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 23 open questions, the oldest 41 days. After: under 5 open, none older than 14 days, after two 20 minute founder rounds.
jobs.who_today: nobody; gaps are filled by guesses

jobs.job: Warn me when a data feed breaks so no number goes quietly stale
jobs.why: When the Shopify, Meta or email feed stops, pages keep showing last week's numbers as if they were today's. Decisions made on stale numbers are wrong in ways no one sees.

watch.metric: expected data pulls that succeeded, by source, 7 days

drives.metric: key numbers shown as unavailable instead of wrong

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the Klaviyo feed missed 5 of its last 7 pulls and no one noticed. After: an alert on the first miss; affected numbers show as unavailable until it is fixed.
jobs.who_today: nobody, or an analyst who spots it late

jobs.job: Tell me how old each fact is so no one acts on one that is out of date
jobs.why: A shipping promise confirmed a year ago may no longer be true. Knowing the age of each fact tells the team which ones to trust and which to check first.

watch.metric: days since each fact was last confirmed, median and oldest

drives.metric: share of facts confirmed in the last 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the median fact is 140 days old and 18 facts are over a year old. After: median under 60 days; nothing older than 180 days without a flag.
jobs.who_today: nobody

jobs.job: Keep product facts right: sizes, materials, care and what ships in the box
jobs.why: When an ad or page says the wrong material or size range, the customer gets something they did not expect and sends it back. Returns eat the margin on that order and the next.

watch.metric: product fact fields missing or in conflict with the Shopify catalog, count
watch.source: brand brain checked against Shopify products

drives.metric: returns with reason not as described, share of orders, 60 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 14 product facts are missing or conflict across 40 products. After: 0 conflicts; 'not as described' returns fall from 3.2% to under 2% over 60 days.
jobs.who_today: merchandiser or founder, in the product admin

jobs.job: Learn from every rejection so agents stop making the same mistake twice
jobs.why: If a founder rejects a draft for being too salesy and the next draft is salesy again, the founder stops trusting the system. Each rejection reason should change what agents do next.

watch.metric: the same rejection reason repeated within 30 days, count

drives.metric: outputs approved on the first pass

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 'too pushy' is the reason on 9 rejections in a month. After: the rule is written into the voice sheet and the reason drops to 1 or 2 a month.
jobs.who_today: founder, by repeating the same notes

jobs.job: Settle where two sources disagree before anyone uses either
jobs.why: A brand deck says 'made in USA' and the site says 'designed in USA'. Someone has to pick which one is true before it goes in an ad, or the brand says both.

watch.metric: unresolved conflicts between sources, count and oldest in days

drives.metric: outputs rejected for a wrong fact

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 5 open conflicts, the oldest 33 days. After: each conflict resolved within 7 days; the site wins by default until the founder rules.
jobs.who_today: nobody

jobs.job: Check that each page carries the disclosures the law requires in each market before it goes live
jobs.why: A missing auto renew notice, return policy or paid partner label can bring a regulator letter or a wave of chargebacks. It is cheap to check before launch and costly after.

watch.metric: live pages missing a required disclosure (US by default: FTC, auto renewal, privacy, returns), share of pages checked
watch.source: brand brain disclosure checklist against site pages

drives.metric: chargebacks citing unclear terms, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 3 of 20 key pages miss a required line. After: 0 of 20; new pages cannot go live until the check passes.
jobs.who_today: lawyer on call, or nobody

jobs.job: Get a new hire or agency working to our standard in a day, not a month
jobs.why: A new freelancer spends weeks learning what we say, what we never say and what we tried. Most of it lives in old chats. Every week of learning is a week of drafts the founder rewrites.

watch.metric: days from access to first approved deliverable

drives.metric: outputs approved on the first pass in the first 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the last agency took 26 days to ship an approved ad. After: under 5 days, working from the one page brand summary.
jobs.who_today: founder, through calls and old decks

jobs.job: Keep the brand voice written down with real examples, so copy sounds like us
jobs.why: Without a voice sheet, every writer invents a tone and the brand sounds different in every channel. Customers notice when an email sounds like a different company from the ad.

watch.metric: drafts rejected for tone, share of reviewed drafts, 30 days

drives.metric: outputs approved on the first pass

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 18% of drafts fail on tone and the voice sheet has 3 examples. After: under 6%, with 20 tagged good and bad examples on file.
jobs.who_today: founder or brand lead

jobs.job: Keep every proof piece findable with its source, date and permission
jobs.why: Reviews, press quotes, awards and test results sell. When no one can find the source or the customer's consent, they either go unused or get used without permission.

watch.metric: proof items on file with source, date and permission recorded, share

drives.metric: share of live claims backed by proof on file

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 40 proof items, 22 with a source and permission. After: 60 items, all with source, date and consent.
jobs.who_today: founder's inbox and a shared drive

jobs.job: Keep the facts for each country we sell in: currency, tax, shipping promise and key dates
jobs.why: A US shipping promise shown to a Canadian shopper, or a holiday sale planned on the wrong date, costs orders and trust. Each market needs its own facts.

watch.metric: countries sold in with complete market facts, share
watch.source: brand brain market fields, countries from Shopify orders

drives.metric: revenue from countries with a correct shipping promise on site

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 2 of 4 countries have complete facts; Canada shows the US delivery time. After: 4 of 4 complete and matched to the site.
jobs.who_today: founder or operations lead

jobs.job: Flag vendor and platform contracts before they renew on their own
jobs.why: Apps, agencies and suppliers renew quietly on old terms. A 60 day warning is the difference between a renegotiation and another year at the old price.

watch.metric: contracts renewing in the next 60 days with no review, count

drives.metric: monthly spend on software, agencies and services

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 3 contracts renew in 60 days, $1,900 a month in total, none reviewed. After: each reviewed 45 days out; 1 cut, 1 renegotiated.
jobs.who_today: founder or bookkeeper, by calendar reminders

jobs.job: Keep marketplace listings matching our own price and claims
jobs.why: When an Amazon or Walmart listing shows a lower price or an old claim, it undercuts the site and confuses shoppers. It can also break the brand's own price rules.

watch.metric: marketplace listings that differ from the brand's price or approved claims, count, weekly
watch.source: marketplace seller tools checked against the brand brain

drives.metric: site conversion rate on products also sold on marketplaces

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 6 listings differ, 2 priced 15% below the site. After: 0 open differences each week; unknown sellers flagged the day they appear.
jobs.who_today: marketplace manager, or nobody

jobs.job: Control who can see which part of the brand's record
jobs.why: Costs, margins and supplier names are private. An agency writing ads does not need them, and a freelancer who leaves should lose access the same day.

watch.metric: brain sections with no written access rule, count

drives.metric: people with access to cost and margin facts

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 9 of 22 sections have no access rule and 4 past freelancers can still read costs. After: every section has a rule; past people removed.
jobs.who_today: nobody

jobs.job: Keep the brand's visual rules and real product photos where every designer pulls from
jobs.why: Designers who cannot find the logo files, colors or real product shots use old or redrawn ones. Off-brand visuals get sent back or, worse, go live.

watch.metric: creatives rejected for off-brand visuals, share, 30 days

drives.metric: hours of creative rework per month (proxy: rejected creatives)

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 1 in 5 creatives fails on visuals. After: under 1 in 12, with the asset kit and approved photos in one place.
jobs.who_today: designer's own folder

jobs.job: Let me take the whole record with me if we part ways with an agency
jobs.why: Years of decisions, tests and approved copy often sit inside an agency's tools. If the relationship ends, the brand should keep all of it in one clean export.

watch.metric: date of last successful full export, and share of sections included

drives.metric: days to get a new agency working after a switch

jobs.now_after: Example: Now no export has ever been tested. After: a full export tested each quarter, 22 of 22 sections included.
jobs.who_today: nobody

jobs.job: Tie each belief about our customers to the data or test behind it
jobs.why: Beliefs like 'our buyers are mostly gift shoppers' steer every ad and page. If no test or data backs them, the whole plan may rest on a guess.

watch.metric: stated customer beliefs with a data source or test on file, share

drives.metric: tests that repeat one already run, count per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 4 of 11 core beliefs have a source. After: 9 of 11, with the 2 others marked as open questions.
jobs.who_today: nobody; lives in the founder's head

jobs.job: Keep the words customers use for the product on file for every writer
jobs.why: Copy written in the customer's own words sells better than copy written in ours. Those words are in reviews and tickets, but no writer has time to read them all.

watch.metric: top products with tagged customer phrases on file, share
watch.source: brand brain, fed from reviews and Gorgias tickets

drives.metric: outputs approved on the first pass

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 2 of 10 top products have customer phrases on file. After: 10 of 10, each with 15 or more tagged phrases.
jobs.who_today: copywriter, one project at a time

jobs.job: Keep dated facts on competitors so no one compares us against old numbers
jobs.why: A comparison built on a rival's price from last year is wrong and can be a legal problem. Each competitor fact needs a date and a source.

watch.metric: days since each competitor was last checked

drives.metric: comparison claims with a dated source, share

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 3 of 7 competitors were last checked over 90 days ago. After: all 7 checked in the last 30 days.
jobs.who_today: founder or agency, now and then
